NONE: › clearly expressed and easy to understand, or (of a person) thinking or speaking clearly
清晰的，明瞭的；（人）頭腦清醒的，說話清楚的

example: She gave a clear and lucid account of her plans for the company's future.
她清楚明瞭地講述了自己對公司未來的規劃。
The drugs she's taking make her drowsy and confused, but there are times when she's quite lucid.
她吃的藥會讓她感到頭暈、意識模糊，但有時頭腦卻很清醒。

NONE: › another name for Satan (= a powerful evil force and the enemy of God)
› a brand name for a type of transparent plastic used to make paints and decorative objects such as picture frames
盧塞特樹酯，人造螢光樹脂（一種用於生產油漆和畫框之類裝飾物的透明塑膠）
A2 the force that causes things, especially good things, to happen to you by chance and not as a result of your own efforts or abilities

example: It was just luck that I asked for a job at the right time.
真是機緣巧合，我剛好在合適的時機開口說想找份工作。
Then I met this gorgeous woman and I couldn't believe my luck.
後來我碰到了這個美麗的女人，我不敢相信自己的運氣有這麽好。
She wears a charm that she thinks brings her good luck.
她戴了一個她認為會給自己帶來好運的護身符。
He seems to have had a lot of bad luck in his life.
他生活中似乎遇到了不少倒霉的事情。
So your interview's tomorrow? Good luck!
這麼說明天你要去面試？祝你好運！
The best of luck in/with your exams!
祝你考試順利！
Have you had any luck with booking your flight?
你訂到飛機票了嗎？
He tried to get into teacher training college but with no luck.
他想進教師進修學院，但未能如願。

NONE: › to get something that you want by chance

example: We lucked into tickets for the World Cup finals.
我們幸運地弄到了世界盃決賽的門票。
The Giants really lucked out in last night's game.
巨人隊在昨晚的比賽中真走運。
Luckily, I had some money with me.
幸好我身上帶了些錢。

NONE: › used to describe someone who has a lot of bad luck

example: The luckless defender, Mark Emery, sustained his third injury of the season.
後衛馬克‧愛默里很不走運，他在本賽季已經是第三次受傷了。

NONE: A2 having good things happen to you by chance
幸運的，走運的，運氣好的

example: "I'm going to Japan." "Lucky you!"
「我要去日本了。」「你運氣真好！」
The lucky winner will be able to choose from three different holidays.
幸運的獲勝者可以從三種不同的假日方案中選擇一種。
[ + to infinitive ] They're lucky to have such a nice office to work in.
他們能在這麽好的辦公室裡工作真走運。
He's lucky that he wasn't fired.
他很幸運，沒有被解僱。
It sounds as if you had a lucky escape (= by good chance you were able to avoid something dangerous or unpleasant).
聽起來好像你是僥倖逃脫啊。
We'll be lucky if we get there by midnight at this rate (= we might get there by midnight or it might be later).
按照這樣的速度，我們能在午夜前到達就算幸運了。
a lucky charm
帶來好運的幸運符
Six is my lucky number.
六是我的幸運數字。

NONE: › a game in which you pay to pick a prize out of a container with many different prizes in it, without being able to see what you are picking
C2 (especially of a business, job, or activity) producing a lot of money
（尤指生意、職位或活動）賺錢的，盈利的

example: The merger proved to be very lucrative for both companies.
事實證明，這次兼併使兩間公司都獲利豐厚。
filthy lucre
不義之財
